name: Blantyre CBD
description: The original commercial core around Victoria Avenue and Haile Selassie Road, with the banks, the offices and St Michael and All Angels Church, built by missionaries in 1888 without an architect. It is busy by day and empties in the evening.
bestFor: Anyone needing banks, offices and the city's institutions
pros: All administrative and banking business is here
St Michael and All Angels is remarkable
Minibuses to the whole city from here
cons: Deserted and best avoided after dark

name: Nyambadwe and Mount Pleasant
description: Residential districts on the higher ground north of the centre, with larger houses, gardens and views across the city towards the Michiru and Ndirande mountains. This is where most of the expatriate and professional population lives.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting space, security and a garden
pros: Cooler air and views over the city

name: Limbe
tagline: The twin town eight kilometres east
description: Blantyre's other half, a separate commercial town eight kilometres away that grew around the railway and the tobacco auction floors. It is busier and rougher than the CBD, with the largest market in the south of the country.
bestFor: Budget stays wanting the market and local prices
pros: The biggest market in southern Malawi
Cheapest rents in the metro area
The railway and tobacco auction floors

name: Namiwawa and Sunnyside
tagline: The leafy middle, between the centre and the hills
description: Established residential suburbs between the CBD and the higher ground, with mature gardens, a good deal of tree cover and much of the city's better rental stock. Chichiri Shopping Centre and the Museum of Malawi are nearby.
bestFor: Anyone wanting a quiet street with the shops within reach
pros: Good rental stock and mature gardens
Chichiri Shopping Centre and the museum
cons: Still needs a car for most errands

name: Mulanje
tagline: Ninety minutes east, under the massif
description: The town at the foot of Mount Mulanje, whose Sapitwa peak at just over three thousand metres is the highest in central Africa. Tea estates surround it and the massif behind is walked hut to hut over several days.
bestFor: Anyone whose reason for being here is the mountain
pros: The best hiking in central Africa
Tea estates and cool highland air
cons: Weather on the massif changes fast
